subject: NIMBUS MAP: econ certification and unit-econ checks
summary: Mutual action plan and econ certification for Nimbus POC. Focused checks on tokens/$, caching and batching assumptions; internal cost sensitivity and final MAP shared with customer.
messages:
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@nimbus.health>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nimbus.health>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MAP outline and cost assumptions

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the call this morning. Before we lock the MAP, procurement asked us to get a quick written confirmation on the unit economics assumptions you’re using for the POC. Specifically:

- Expected tokens per inference (prompt + generated): ?
- Assumed tokens/$ (for hosted eval vs dedicated)
- Whether prefix/KV caching reduces billable tokens for repeated prompts
- Typical batching assumptions for sub-200ms SLOs

Can you put the assumptions in writing and flag any sensitivities that would materially change cost at scale? We need this to justify budget to finance.

Also looping in our tech lead Sid to confirm traffic shape.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Jones
Head of Product, Nimbus Health
alex.jones@nimbus.health

--

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@nimbus.health>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial MAP outline and cost assumptions

Alex —

Appreciate the concretes. I’ve attached a short token-econ CSV and a first-pass MAP (nimbus_map_v1.xlsx). Key assumptions below — these are the numbers we’ll certify for the POC and include in the MAP deliverables unless you ask for changes: 

1) Baseline request profile (from your traffic sample):
   - Median prompt tokens: 85
   - Median generation tokens: 95
   - Avg tokens per call: 180

2) Pricing assumptions (hosted evaluation tier):
   - Redwood hosted eval price used for MAP: $0.80 per 1M tokens (i.e. $0.0008 / 1k tokens)
   - Equivalent tokens/$ = 1,250,000 tokens per $1k; for easier math: 1.25M tokens per $1k

3) Caching assumptions:
   - Prefix caching expected to reduce billable tokens for repeated prompts by ~35% for the 40% of traffic identified as template-driven (e.g., triage prompts).
   - KV cache hits (session-level) reduce generation work but do not change billed prompt tokens; model-level prefix caching reflected in token-econ spreadsheet.

4) Batching assumptions and SLOs:
   - P99 latency target: 250ms (internal acceptance target for POC: 300ms).
   - For 250ms P99 and your traffic mix, we model an effective batching factor of 1.6 on average (some micro-batching at 2–4 for low-rate bursts).
   - Batching reduces per-token cost by ~12% vs single-call baseline in our runtime model.

5) Sensitivities (what moves cost materially):
   - Average generation length +50 tokens => +28% per-call cost
   - Caching hit rate +/-10% => +/-8% cost swing
   - Batching factor drop to 1.0 (no batching) => +12% cost

I’ve also included a conservative and aggressive column in token-econ-model.csv so you can see a 10/50/90 percentile impact. If you’d like, Rishi and I can run a short tabletop using your 48-hour sample to generate a MAP-certified cost number.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm if the 180 tokens/call baseline looks right to Sid.
- We run the 48-hour sample through our model (2 business days) and update the MAP numbers with a certified expected spend for the POC window.
- Procurement and finance sign-off on the MAP numbers; we include credit guardrails if the POC exceeds expected profile.

Attaching: token-econ-model.csv, nimbus_map_v1.xlsx

Best,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0168

Attachment stubs: token-econ-model.csv (CSV), nimbus_map_v1.xlsx (Excel)

From: Sid Patel <sid.patel@nimbus.health>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@nimbus.health>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbus.health <procurement@nimbus.health>
Date: 2026-10-20T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MAP outline and cost assumptions

Thanks — quick clarification from our side on traffic shape:
- ~52% of calls are templated (same prompt structure, different patient ids)
- ~30% are short queries (prompt + 20–40 generation tokens)
- Peak TPS expected during morning batch windows: 45 TPS for 5–10 minutes

If prefix caching only reduces billable prompt tokens but not generation, the 35% number seems reasonable, maybe conservative. For batching — we are worried about latency during peak TPS bursts. Can Redwood run burst-only routing to dedicated faster capacity if we hit >40 TPS?

Sid
Principal Engineer, Nimbus Health

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: sensitivity and routing options for Nimbus MAP

Olga / Monica —

Quick internal notes to prepare the certified numbers before we run the 48-hour sample:

- For the POC we should provide two cost envelopes: "POC baseline" (assumes 180 tokens/call, 35% caching hit, batching factor 1.6) and "POC+burst" which gates jump to Dedicated fast-path above 40 TPS.
- Routing: implement policy in MAP: hosted evaluation until sustained 40 TPS/5min -> auto-route burst to Dedicated with agreed cost uplift of +18% per-token equivalent (covers reserved capacity overhead). Document the auto-fallback in the MAP.
- Credits/guardrails: propose a $5k overage credit for first month of POC if actual spend > 120% of forecast and we did not deviate from traffic profile.

Numbers I ran quickly (attached token-econ-model.csv has the details):
- Baseline monthlyized for POC (30-day equivalent, scaled to expected 150k calls/day):~ $2,100 (hosted, with caching and batching)
- If caching hit drops to 25% => ~$2,270 (+8%)
- If average generation increases +50 tokens => ~$2,700 (+28%)
- If bursts routed to Dedicated for 6 hours/day => incremental $950/day for those hours (dedicated cost uplift)

Monica: can you sanity-check the dedicated uplift number? The finance ask next week will want to see both options side-by-side.

-Rishi
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@nimbus.health>, sid.patel@nimbus.health
Cc: procurement@nimbus.health <procurement@nimbus.health>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial MAP outline and cost assumptions — certified MAP v1

Alex / Sid / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick answers. Per our internal run (attached files) we certify the following POC MAP assumptions for Nimbus (MAP v1 attached):

Certified assumptions (MAP v1):
- Baseline avg tokens/call: 180 (85 prompt / 95 generation)
- Effective tokens/$ (hosted eval rate used): $0.80 per 1M tokens (0.0008 / 1k)
- Caching: prefix caching hit 35% for templated traffic (documented in worksheet) => realized billable tokens down ~12% across total traffic
- Batching: avg batching factor 1.6, expected batching benefit ~12% cost reduction
- Burst policy: auto-route to Dedicated when sustained >40 TPS for >=5 minutes. Dedicated uplift: +18% token-equivalent cost. Details in MAP doc (section 3).
- Guardrail: $5k overage credit for the first POC month if spend >120% of forecast and traffic adheres to sampled profile.

Attached: nimbus_map_v1.xlsx (MAP with rollout and acceptance criteria), token-econ-model.csv (certified numbers), redwood-soc2-evidence-list.pdf (requested by procurement)

Next actions:
1) Alex — please confirm final approval from Procurement on the MAP numbers so we can push a signed MAP + DocuSign.
2) Sid — if you can drop the 48-hour sample by EOD Monday we’ll run it against the model and produce MAP v1.1 with per-segment certified spend.
3) We’ll schedule a 30-min signoff call after procurement review.

If procurement wants any alternate uplift bands for dedicated or a different credit structure, we can add as an appendix to the MAP.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: nimbus_map_v1.xlsx, token-econ-model.csv, redwood-soc2-evidence-list.pdf
